investigations.title: Same position one turn later is a different stroke
investigations.objective: Observe that identical piston position one turn apart shows different valve states.
investigations.explanation: Same crank-pin position returns after 360 deg, but valves differ: intake open at 90 deg versus both closed at 450 deg, so the first return is not the same stroke in the four-stroke sequence.
investigations.sourceQuote: One cycle = four piston strokes = two crankshaft turns (720°).

investigations.title: Two upstrokes differ by valve state
investigations.objective: Compare the two upward strokes to see closed valves versus open exhaust valve.
investigations.explanation: Both are upward mid-strokes with matching piston and rod geometry, but compression has both valves closed while exhaust has exhaust open, showing different gas exchange roles.
investigations.sourceQuote: 4. Exhaust: piston up; exhaust open; burnt gas leaves.

investigations.title: Rod links piston pin to crank pin
investigations.objective: Inspect the connecting rod linking piston pin to crank pin at mid-stroke.
investigations.explanation: At mid-power the rod is angled between the piston pin above and the crank pin to the side, visibly linking vertical piston motion to crank rotation.
investigations.sourceQuote: Connecting rod joins piston pin to crank pin throughout.
